newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA ADOPTS DECLARATION ON NATO BID.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA ADOPTS DECLARATION ON NATO BID.

text.p: Bulgaria's caretaker government on Monday adopted a declaration stating a desire for a full NATO membership in bid to clear the country's so far ambiguous policy on the issue, said foreign Minister Stoyan Stalev.
"The cabinet adopted a declaration in which it clearly states its will for a full NATO membership," Stalev told reporters.

The declaration, endorsed by Bulgaria's head of state Petar Stoyanov, aims to qualify the Balkan country for membership nomination at a NATO summit in July, where the alliance would decide which new members to admit.
In the declaration, shortly to be presented to NATO headquarters, Bulgaria states its will to be invited for accession talks, said Stalev.

Despite a parliamentary declaration stating its will to join the alliance passed in 1993, the ruling Socialists in the past two years have obscured the issue for fear of obsetting Russia, which opposes the eastward expansion of NATO.

The Socialists stepped down from power two weeks ago and 20 months before the end of their term, bowing to opposition demands for early election after 30 days of mass protests fueled by economic hardship.
Stoyanov, elected on the opposition ticket in November, appointed a caretaker government last week and set elections for April 19.
Bulgaria is a member of the Partnership for Peace Programme designed to forge closer ties between NATO and the ex-communist states.
